Return a concise report (≤ 700 words) with concrete recommendations, hex codes, and URLs to sources/references. Don't fabricate.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

Reach for this when the task matches an available agent type, when you have independent work to run in parallel, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate it and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps. For a single-fact lookup where you already know the file, symbol, or value, search directly. Once you've delegated a search, don't also run it yourself — wait for the result.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.

- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

## Cozy theme research for the learning app

**1. What makes a UI feel cozy**
- **Shape and surface:** generous corner radii (16–28px on cards, fully rounded pill buttons), soft diffuse shadows, soft pastel surfaces with dark readable text. Keep the brightest color for the one active element ([Playful Rounded kit](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@wrongstack/core@0.295.1/design-kits/playful-rounded/KIT.md), [daisyUI claymorphism](https://trends.daisyui.com/trend/claymorphism/)).
- **Low stakes:** cozy games are defined by soft visuals, low risk and easy exits ([Replay journal, 2024](https://czasopisma.uni.lodz.pl/Replay/article/download/24071/24087/59119)). Clutter breaks the calm ([SDLC Corp](https://sdlccorp.com/post/the-art-of-designing-intuitive-user-interfaces-in-cozy-games/)). For this app that means no punitive red states, a "gentle error" color, and failure framed as "try again".
- **Products to borrow from:** Headspace (rounded shapes, slow easing), Duolingo (chunky progress bar, celebration only at milestones), Linear and Arc (restraint, tinted neutrals, one accent color), Animal Crossing (pill-shaped speech bubbles for chat).
- **Never pure #000 or #FFF for large areas:** use slightly tinted neutrals.
- **Motion:** 150–300ms ease-out, nothing that loops, and respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.

**2. Default palette ("Frost": light blue / white / silver)**
I calculated these contrast ratios myself with the WCAG formula.

| Token | Hex | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| background | `#F4F8FB` | cool off-white |
| surface (cards, chat bubbles, input) | `#FFFFFF` | |
| surface-2 / silver | `#E8EEF3` | tabs, hover states |
| border / silver | `#D3DCE5` | decorative only |
| primary | `#2F6FAF` | white text on it 5.23:1, passes AA |
| primary-soft | `#DCEBF7` | selected and highlight fill; text on it 11.9:1 |
| accent (sky) | `#7FB3E0` | decorative only (2.2:1): XP fill, glows |
| text | `#1E2A3A` | 13.6:1 on background |
| muted text | `#5A6B7D` | 5.13:1 on background, 5.48:1 on white |
| success | `#2E7D5B` | 5.0:1 on white |
| gentle error | `#B5524A` | 4.92:1 on white |

- Don't use `#3A7BBF` as a button color: it only reaches 4.41:1 and fails AA.
- Silver tones (`#A9B6C4`, 2.06:1) must never carry text.

**Unlockable theme ideas** (background / surface / primary / accent; check text contrast for each one in code):
- **Sunset:** `#FFF4EC` / `#FFFFFF` / `#C2553A` / `#F4A261`
- **Forest:** `#F1F5EE` / `#FBFCF9` / `#3F6B4A` / `#A3C49A`
- **Sakura:** `#FDF3F5` / `#FFFFFF` / `#B04A6B` / `#F5B8C8`
- **Parchment / RPG:** `#F5ECD7` / `#FBF5E6` / `#7A4E2D` / `#C9A227`, with a serif display font
- **Night Sky (dark):** `#141B2D` / `#1E2740` / `#8FB8FF` / `#F2D27A`, text `#E6ECF5`
- **Matcha:** `#F3F5EC` / `#FFFFFF` / `#55703B` / `#C5D6A0`

**3. Typography**
- **Recommendation:** **Nunito** for the whole UI. It is rounded, friendly, a variable font, and reads well at chat sizes ([Google Fonts](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Nunito)).
- **Optional:** **Fraunces** for headings in the Parchment theme ([Google Fonts](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Fraunces)).
- **Alternative:** offer **Lexend**, which was designed for reading proficiency ([Google Fonts](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Lexend)), as a readability toggle.
- **Avoid:** Quicksand for body text; it is too thin at small sizes.

**4. Implementation**
- **Tokens and theme switching:** keep semantic CSS variables in `:root` and override them per theme with `[data-theme="sunset"]{...}`. Map them into Tailwind v4 with `@theme inline { --color-background: var(--background); ... }` so utilities like `bg-primary` follow the active theme ([Tailwind theme docs](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/theme)).
- **Dark variant:** for Night Sky, add `@custom-variant dark (&:where([data-theme="night"], [data-theme="night"] *));` ([Tailwind dark mode docs](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/dark-mode)).
- **shadcn/ui:** it already uses exactly these names (`--background`, `--primary`, `--muted-foreground`, `--radius`, and so on) in OKLCH plus `@theme inline` ([shadcn theming docs](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/theming)). Each theme is then just one CSS block. Set `--radius: 1rem` for the cozy look.
- **Registry for locking and unlocking:** keep one typed array, `THEMES = [{id, name, unlock: {sessions: n}, swatch: [...]}]`. Store the user's unlocked IDs and selected theme in localStorage or the DB, and set `document.documentElement.dataset.theme`.
- **Locked themes:** show as grayed-out swatches with a padlock and a hint like "Complete 3 sessions".
- **Adding a theme:** one CSS block plus one array entry.
- **Avoiding a theme flash:** set `data-theme` in an inline `<head>` script before the page renders.

**Motion libraries**
- **Motion** (formerly Framer Motion, [motion.dev](https://motion.dev)): use `LazyMotion` with `m` components to keep the bundle small ([bundle-size guide](https://motion.dev/docs/react-reduce-bundle-size)). Good for XP bar springs and layout transitions.
- **canvas-confetti:** tiny, and its `disableForReducedMotion` option turns confetti off entirely for users who prefer reduced motion ([GitHub](https://github.com/catdad/canvas-confetti)). Use it only for session completion and theme unlocks.
- **Lottie:** skip it. The player is heavy and needs designed assets.

**5. Gamification without clutter**
- **XP bar:** a thin (6–8px) rounded bar under the top tabs, accent fill, spring animation on gain, and a small "+20 XP" chip that fades out.
- **Session progress:** a row of 5–10 dots or a segmented bar rather than percentages.
- **Boss health bar:** used only in "boss" review rounds. A rounded bar with a cute icon that "shakes" gently (2px, 200ms) on a correct answer; never flash red at the user.
- **Section map:** a vertical winding path of circular nodes, Duolingo-style, in its own tab rather than in the chat view. Completed nodes are filled primary, the current node has a soft pulsing ring, locked nodes are silver.
- **Rewards:** a theme unlock gets a toast card ("New theme: Sakura") with a "Try it" button.
- **Overall rule:** at most one celebratory effect per milestone, and the chat area itself stays clean.
